readout_other: Coma Recovery Scale-Revised (CRS-R index); BOLD fMRI during sonication; psychophysiological interaction connectivity
direction_notes: BOLD signal decreased in frontal cortex and striatum during sonication; CRS-R responsiveness rose in the week after LIFU versus baseline, with no sham control.
safety_notes: Vital signs unchanged during LIFU; two adverse events (respiratory suppression before any LIFU; a seizure more than a week later with sepsis) were judged unrelated to LIFU.

timing.protocol_description: Ten 30 s sonication blocks on, separated by 30 s off-periods, delivered inside the MRI; one LIFU session, or two sessions one week apart in some patients.

source_quotes.n_subjects: This study included 11 acute DOC patients (see Table 1 for details).
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: Four patients, who were in the care of the Ronald Reagan UCLA Medical Center for longer periods, underwent the procedure twice, with 1 week separating each LIFU administration.

flags.reason: Text says a second session was possible for 27% of the sample and elsewhere says 3 patients had 2 runs; Table 1 and the Methods say four patients had two sessions.

Intensities are stated as ISPPA.3 and ISPTA.3, derated with 0.3 dB/cm-MHz tissue absorption; the paper gives 719.73 mW/cm2 for ISPTA.3, recorded as 0.71973 W/cm2. Treated as derated values; whether skull attenuation is included is not stated.
One patient had glioma/stroke etiology; the others traumatic brain injury (Table 1).
Target is the central thalamus, intended on the left; the beam is long (about 1.5 cm) and also reaches basal ganglia. Right thalamus was sonicated in some patients (Table 1).
